title: Vox MCP Server Registry
description: Shape of config/mcp.toml once parsed by tomllib. MCP servers are external subprocesses that expose arbitrary tools, so this contract exists before the client does -- the same order policy.py came before any tool that needed it. There is deliberately no key for a credential: a secret reaches a server only by naming an environment variable in env_passthrough, and the value is still read from the environment.

enabled.description: Master switch. Ships false: an MCP server can do anything its tools can do, so it is opt-in twice (here and per server).

require_confirmation.description: Whether a remote tool needs an explicit user confirmation before each run. Ships true; a per-server auto_allow list is the only way to narrow it.

name.description: Lowercase slug. It becomes part of the tool name (mcp.<name>.<tool>), so the character set is restricted rather than free text.

allow.description: Remote tool names this server may expose. Empty means all of them, which is the widest setting and is why it is worth writing down.

auto_allow.description: Remote tool names that run without a per-call confirmation. Empty means every call is confirmed.
